target_audience: Advanced High School (AP Calculus) or First-year University Students

sections.title: The Mystery of the Tangled Equation
lecture_lines: Explicit functions keep y isolated on one side.
Implicit equations mix x and y together.
Take this circle: solving for y creates messy roots.
Yet, every point on this curve has a slope.
Implicit differentiation reveals slope without isolating y.
animations: Create expressions 'y = 2x + 1' (Blue: #58C4DD) and 'x^2 + y^2 = 25' (Yellow: #FFFF00) at top.
Animate a pulsing white circle around 'y' in 'y = 2x + 1' to show isolation.
Draw a large yellow circle (#FFFF00) centered on the screen for 'x^2 + y^2 = 25'.
Show the text 'y = \pm \sqrt{25 - x^2}' appearing then covered by a red 'X' (#FF0000).
Display a large white question mark '?' at the center of the circle curve.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Chain Rule Secret
lecture_lines: Treat y as an invisible function of x.
Derivative of y-cubed isn't just three y-squared.
We must multiply by the inner derivative, dy dx.
animations: Display the chain rule formula: d/dx [f(x)^3] = 3f(x)^2 \cdot f'(x).
Transform the formula into d/dx [y^3] = 3y^2 \cdot (dy/dx) by replacing f(x) with y.
Highlight (dy/dx) in bright red (#FF0000) and label it 'Inner Derivative Footprint'.

sections.title: Step 1: The 'Differentiate Both Sides' Blitz
lecture_lines: Apply the derivative operator to every single term.
Power rule handles x-squared normally, giving two x.
For y-squared, the chain rule adds dy dx.
The derivative of a constant, twenty-five, is zero.
Our equation now links x, y, and slope.
animations: Display the full equation x^2 + y^2 = 25 in the center.
Animate 'd/dx' operators appearing in front of each term on both sides.
Transform 'd/dx(x^2)' into '2x' using blue color (#58C4DD).
Transform 'd/dx(y^2)' into '2y \cdot (dy/dx)', with 'dy/dx' in red (#FF0000).
Simplify the equation view to 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0.

sections.title: Step 2: Isolating the Target (dy/dx)
lecture_lines: We begin with our differentiated equation.
Subtract two x to move it across the equals.
Divide by two y to solve for dy dx.
animations: Display the equation '2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0' and highlight '(dy/dx)' in red (#FF0000).
Shift '2x' to the right side of the equals sign, changing its sign to '-2x'.
Algebraically move '2y' to the denominator of the right side, forming '(dy/dx) = -2x / 2y'.
Strike through the '2' in both the numerator and denominator using a thin red line (#FF0000).
Surround the simplified result 'dy/dx = -x/y' with a green box (#83C167).

sections.title: Visual Validation: The Radar Cat
lecture_lines: Let's look at point three-four on the circle.
Our derivative gives a slope of negative three-fourths.
This tangent line visually confirms the downward slope.
At point zero-five, the calculated slope is zero.
The horizontal tangent matches the top of the curve.
animations: On the yellow circle (#FFFF00), highlight (3, 4) and show calculation 'dy/dx = -3/4' in red (#FF0000).
Highlight the point (0, 5) and show the calculation 'dy/dx = -0/5 = 0' in blue (#58C4DD).
Draw a red tangent line through (3, 4) and a blue horizontal tangent line through (0, 5).

sections.title: Summary & Mastery Recap
lecture_lines: First, differentiate every term, using the chain rule.
Next, use algebra to solve for dy dx.
Now you can find slopes for any tangled curve.
animations: Show a numbered list: 1. Differentiate, 2. Isolate dy/dx, 3. Solve for slope.
Display a complex figure-8 (Lissajous) curve with several tangent arrows.
Show concluding text 'Implicit Differentiation: Unlocking Hidden Curves' in gold (#FFD700).
